cohort: The study included 488 adolescent and adult mothers who gave birth at 28 or more weeks of gestation in North Wollo Zone Public Hospitals, Northern Ethiopia.
finding: Adolescent mothers exhibited significantly higher rates of adverse obstetrical outcomes compared to adult mothers, including preterm labor, antepartum hemorrhage, anemia, pregnancy-induced hypertension, malpresentation, cephalopelvic disproportion, major perineal tears, and cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Adolescent mothers had a significantly higher rate of cesarean delivery (16.0% vs. 9.8%, p = 0.04) compared to adult mothers.
